propositions.text: This judicial review challenges the Refugee Protection Division's decision rejecting the applicant's asylum claim as manifestly unfounded under section 107(2) of the IRPA.
I orally ruled the RPD's decision unreasonable and granted the judicial review application.
These are the reasons for my judgment.

paragraphs.summary: The court states the judicial review challenges the RPD's rejection of the applicant's asylum claim as manifestly unfounded, grants the review, and provides reasons.

propositions.text: The applicant is a Cuban citizen who alleges certain facts.

paragraphs.summary: The court states the applicant is a Cuban citizen who alleges facts.

propositions.text: In October 2011, the applicant was fired from his hotel security supervisor job.
The security chief fired him due to a theft during his supervision.
The applicant believes he was fired because he told the security chief communism was a lie and opposed Cuba's policies and human rights abuses.

paragraphs.summary: The applicant alleges he was fired in October 2011 due to his political opinions, not the theft at the hotel.

propositions.text: In December 2011, police searched the applicant's home and confiscated jewelry for his business.
Police took the applicant for questioning, during which he was beaten, mistreated, threatened, and fined 50 pesos before release.

paragraphs.summary: The applicant states police searched his home, confiscated jewelry, mistreated him during questioning, and fined him 50 pesos in December 2011.

propositions.text: Between 2012 and 2013, police repeatedly searched the applicant's home and arrested him for protesting government and police abuses.
The applicant and family were threatened with imprisonment; his daughter was mistreated at school for refusing patriotic acts and being seen as an opponent's child.

paragraphs.summary: The applicant alleges repeated police searches, arrests for protests, threats to family, and mistreatment of his daughter at school.

propositions.text: Due to harassment, the applicant moved his family to the countryside with his farmer brothers.
Local police threatened him after being informed of his prior problems, so the family returned to the municipality.

paragraphs.summary: The applicant moved his family to the countryside but returned due to police threats.

propositions.text: In 2014, the applicant was arrested for attending an opposition meeting and released after paying a 50 peso fine.

paragraphs.summary: The applicant states he was arrested in 2014 for attending an opposition meeting and fined 50 pesos.

propositions.text: From 2015 to 2018, the applicant's home was surveilled and repeatedly searched without warrants by police and technical research agents.
During searches, police confiscated sugar, flour, and oil for his cafeteria business.
The applicant was again arrested, questioned, threatened, and fined 50 pesos before release.

paragraphs.summary: The applicant alleges repeated warrantless searches, confiscations of business goods, arrests, threats, and fines from 2015 to 2018.

propositions.text: In January 2019, police searched the applicant's home with a warrant and seized clothing and shoes for sale.
The applicant was arrested and fined 50 pesos.

paragraphs.summary: In January 2019, the applicant's home was searched with a warrant, items seized, and he was fined 50 pesos.

propositions.text: In March 2019, the applicant was arrested by political police, isolated for interrogation, and warned he would be 'eliminated' if arrested again.

paragraphs.summary: The applicant states he was arrested and threatened with elimination by political police in March 2019.

propositions.text: Fearing the threat, the applicant left Cuba and applied for asylum in Canada on December 19, 2019.
The RPD held a hearing on December 7, 2021, and decided on February 4, 2022, rejecting the applicant's asylum claim as manifestly unfounded under section 107(2) IRPA.
The RPD excluded the applicant from appealing to the Refugee Appeal Division.

paragraphs.summary: The applicant fled Cuba, applied for asylum in 2019; the RPD rejected his claim as manifestly unfounded in 2022 and barred appeal.

propositions.text: I find the RPD's decision unreasonable, citing Canada (Minister of Citizenship and Immigration) v Vavilov, 2019 SCC 65 paras 16-17, 85.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the RPD's decision unreasonable, referencing Vavilov.

propositions.text: The applicant relies on Rahaman v Canada (Minister of Citizenship and Immigration), 2002 FCA 89 para 51, arguing the RPD can only find no credibility after examining all evidence and finding no credible basis for refugee status.
The applicant argues the RPD failed to consider all evidence, including credible evidence, before concluding the claim was manifestly unfounded.

paragraphs.summary: The applicant argues the RPD failed to consider all credible evidence before finding the claim manifestly unfounded, relying on Rahaman.

propositions.text: The applicant contends the RPD did not justify why it believed he was fired for theft rather than political opinions.
The applicant argues the RPD relied on personal views of Cuba's hotel sector without citing objective evidence from the National Documentation Package.
The applicant claims the RPD ignored key allegations of persecution due to opposition to the government, reflecting a deficient analysis of the evidence.

paragraphs.summary: The applicant argues the RPD unjustifiably concluded he was fired for theft, ignored key persecution allegations, and lacked objective evidence.

propositions.text: The respondent argues the no-credibility conclusion was reasonable, based on contradictions in the applicant's testimony about why he was fired.
The respondent contends the applicant gave an implausible story linking government criticism, theft, and police visits, which the tribunal disbelieved.
The respondent submits the overall evidentiary gaps reasonably support the adverse credibility finding.

paragraphs.summary: The respondent argues the adverse credibility finding was reasonable due to contradictions and implausible explanations by the applicant.

propositions.text: I reject the respondent's arguments; the RPD mainly relied on an alleged contradiction about why the applicant was fired to find no credibility.
The applicant did not contradict himself; he mentioned the theft and his disagreement with socialism in his narrative at paragraph 5.

paragraphs.summary: The court rejects the respondent's argument, finding no contradiction in the applicant's testimony about his firing reason.

propositions.text: The alleged contradiction was not revealed during testimony as the RPD noted.
It was unreasonable for the RPD to rely on this non-contradiction to doubt all other allegations without referencing evidence or objective proof.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the RPD unreasonably relied on a non-contradiction to doubt all allegations without evidence.

propositions.text: The RPD found it more likely the applicant was fired for theft and police searched him for illegal goods possession.

While the RPD could reach such a conclusion, it must provide transparent, coherent, and rational reasons given the serious consequences of a no-minimum-basis finding (citing Aquila, 2022 CF 231 para 16).

paragraphs.summary: The court notes the RPD's conclusion but requires transparent, coherent reasons due to serious consequences, citing Aquila.

propositions.text: The RPD claimed it was more probable the applicant was fired for theft because Cuba depends on tourism and hotels must secure tourists.
The RPD cited no objective evidence for this conclusion.
The RPD claimed repeated searches were due to possession of illegal goods because Cuba regulates everything, including food requiring ration coupons.
Again, the RPD cited no objective evidence to support this conclusion.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the RPD made unsupported factual conclusions without objective evidence about theft and illegal goods.

propositions.text: There was evidence the RPD ignored that could corroborate the applicant's allegations, including business licenses for jewelry and cafeteria operations.
Objective evidence in the National Documentation Package shows political opponents are not tolerated and mistreated for dissent or protests, as alleged by the applicant.
Screenshots of the applicant's social media posts show he continued expressing dissenting opinions after leaving Cuba.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the RPD ignored evidence corroborating the applicant's claims, including licenses, objective country evidence, and social media posts.

propositions.text: La SPR n’a pas raisonnablement analysé les éléments de preuve avant de conclure que le demandeur n’était pas crédible
La SPR posait ses questions au demandeur de façon agressive et déroutante
Cette conduite remet en doute si le tribunal voulait considérer le témoignage du demandeur

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker did not reasonably analyze evidence before finding the applicant not credible; the court finds the SPR's questioning was aggressive and undermined consideration of testimony.

propositions.text: La SPR n’a pas justifié comment les faits atteignent le seuil élevé requis pour absence de minimum de fondement
Joseph c Canada (Citoyenneté et Immigration), 2018 CF 638 para 13 sets a high threshold for absence of minimum foundation

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the SPR did not justify meeting the high threshold for absence of minimum foundation, citing Joseph c Canada 2018 CF 638 para 13.

propositions.text: La décision de la SPR n’est pas raisonnable
La demande de contrôle judiciaire est accueillie
Aucune question n’est certifiée
Aucuns dépens ne sont adjugés

paragraphs.summary: The court concludes the SPR decision is unreasonable, grants judicial review, certifies no questions, and awards no costs.
